title: Contingency Capacity & Graceful Degradation Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines the operational runbooks, triggers, and tooling patterns the SRE team uses to protect customer SLAs during acute capacity stress (regional surges, degraded kernel performance, or cross-tenant flash traffic). It focuses on two complementary axes: (1) Capacity hedging & emergency augmentation, and (2) graceful degradation strategies that preserve highest-value traffic while keeping the platform available.

Scope & applicability:

- Applies to Redwood serving plane components: routing layer, model runners (GPU/CPU), KV prefix caches, and the autoscaling controller.
- Scenarios covered: sudden traffic surge, sustained error-budget burn > fast-burn threshold, regional outage, kernel/path regressions that reduce per-GPU throughput, and data-plane misconfiguration causing queueing.
- Not covered: long-term capacity planning (see capacity handbook), billing disputes, or customer-side SDK bugs.

Goals & success metrics:

- Preserve availability for top-tier SLOs during incidents (target: keep P99 latency < 2x baseline for 95% of requests in top-tier routes).
- Maintain fair allocation across customers: no single tenant should consume > 30% of regional burst pool unless explicitly agreed.
- Limit customer-facing errors: aim to keep 95th percentile success-rate >= 99% for critical routes during hedging.
- Documented rollback steps for any mitigation (must be reversible within 5 minutes).

SLO partitioning and error budget policies (summary):

- SLO tiers: 
  - Critical (enterprise dedicated endpoints, SLA-backed): 99.95% availability monthly.
  - Standard (hosted API default): 99.5% availability monthly.
  - Best-effort (background batch/embeddings non-interactive): 99.0% availability monthly.

- Error budget burn policy (examples):
  - If burn rate > 5x expected for 30m on Critical routes -> immediate paging to oncall + activate emergency capacity runbook.
  - If Standard routes exceed 3x burn for 60m -> open incident channel and evaluate degradation strategies.

- Partitioning guidance: SLOs and error budgets must be tracked per-region, per-model-family, and per-customer-tier. Treat model families (chat, text-gen, embeddings) separately for burn calculations.

Capacity triggers and hedging strategies:

- Early signals (automated detectors):
  1) Autoscaling unable to achieve target GPU counts for 5m and regional queue growth > 20%
  2) Mean token throughput per-GPU falls > 25% vs baseline for 10m (indicates kernel/regression)
  3) Latency P95 increases > 2x baseline and error-rate increases > 0.5% absolute

- Automated immediate hedges (executed by platform orchestration):
  - Enable regional burst pool (pre-reserved capacity) and apply per-tenant rate caps to prevent noisy neighbor amplification.
  - Route background embeddings off to cheaper CPU clusters with lower SLOs.
  - Increase KV-prefix cache TTL prioritization for small prompt prefixes to reduce compute per-request.

- Manual/Operator hedges (when automated options insufficient):
  - Toggle fallback routing to smaller model variants (e.g., redwood-gpt-medium -> redwood-gpt-small) for non-enterprise routes via feature-flag.
  - Temporarily lower max tokens or top_k for non-critical routes with a coordinated rollout.
  - Suspend heavy batched jobs or scheduled evals that consume capacity (Coordination with product/ML).

- Hedging fairness and quotas:
  - Burst pool allocation rules: default per-tenant cap = min(10% of pool, 2x baseline rate). Enterprise customers with committed capacity can request exceptions via oncall.
  - If a tenant exceeds 30% of active burst pool for > 5m, auto-throttle to baseline rate and notify account team.

Operational tooling and dashboards:

- Dashboards (must exist and be visible in Console):
  - Regional capacity dashboard: per-GPU utilization, queue sizes, average token/s, model-family throughput (real-time heatmap).
  - Error-budget burn dashboard: live burn-rate with lane filters (region/model-family/customer-tier).
  - Degradation impact simulator: quick view showing estimated customer SLO impact for candidate mitigations (e.g., model-fallback or token-limits).

- Automation & runbook tooling:
  - playbook-cli (internal tool) supports: enable-burst-pool, apply-tenant-throttle, toggle-fallback, prime-cache, and force-deployment-of-quantized-variant.
  - All playbook-cli actions write an audit event to audit-log and create an incident annotation.

Emergency runbook (ordered steps, run-by-run):

1) Triage (T+0 to T+5m)
   - Confirm alert seed (link alert) and open incident channel (PagerDuty + #inc-<service>).
   - Snapshot dashboards: regional capacity + error budget + top-50 routes by QPS.
   - Identify whether cause appears compute (GPU saturation), network (region isolation), or software (kernel regression).

2) Immediate automated mitigations (T+5 to T+10m)
   - playbook-cli enable-burst-pool --region <region> --duration 2h
   - playbook-cli apply-tenant-throttle --scope top-30-traffic --limit 50%
   - If kernel regression suspected: route small/short requests to CPU fallback pool (playbook-cli toggle-fallback --family text-gen --target cpu-fallback).

3) Targeted degradation (T+10 to T+30m) — apply after coordination with incident commander
   - Apply model-size fallback for Standard tier (feature-flag flip, staged 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 10m windows).
   - Reduce max_response_tokens to 128 for best-effort routes; communicate to customers via status page if customer-facing.
   - Turn on aggressive prefix caching: prime most common 10K prefixes using cache-priming job.

4) Capacity augmentation (if hedges insufficient)
   - Activate reserved emergency hosts (reserved_gpus pool) and scale autoscaler scale-up limits (ops-runbook notes exact SKU and zone).
   - Coordinate with cloud provider contacts to request expedited quota growth (ops lead).

5) Stabilization and rollback
   - Track burn-rate and latency windows: when burn-rate falls below 1.2x baseline for 30m, begin staged rollback of degradations in reverse order.
   - Ensure each rollback step has a 10m observation window.

Post-incident review & evidence checklist:

- Minimum artifacts for RCA: incident timeline, alerts and dashboards screenshots, playbook-cli action log (all commands), PRs/deploys around the time window, and a list of customers impacted with severity.
- Classification: root cause (software/regression/hardware/cloud), failure mode (queue buildup, OOM, kernel slow-path), and mitigation effectiveness (time-to-stabilize, customer impact).
- Run a traffic replay for 2x peak workload in staging with the fixes to validate regression remediation.

Runbook examples (concrete CLI examples):

- Enable burst pool (example):
  - playbook-cli enable-burst-pool --region us-west-2 --pool-name reserved-burst-1 --reason "regional surge" --annotate incident-12345

- Apply tenant throttle (example):
  - playbook-cli apply-tenant-throttle --tenant-id all-standard --limit-qps 150 --duration 30m --annotate incident-12345

- Toggle model fallback (example):
  - playbook-cli toggle-fallback --model-family chat --from redwood-chat-large --to redwood-chat-medium --percent 25 --annotate incident-12345

SLO & incident review scoring rubric (for postmortems):

- Impact score: combination of customer-minutes affected and SLO tier.
- Response score: time-to-detect, time-to-initiate-mitigation, time-to-stabilize.
- Stabilization quality: reversibility, data-loss risk, and ability to restore performance without restart.

Ownership, roles, and communication templates:

- Incident commander: senior SRE on pager (coordinate mitigations, approvals for customer-impacting degradations).
- Operator: runs playbook-cli steps and documents actions.
- Customer comms: CS lead drafts status updates; use template: short summary, impacted regions/models, mitigation in place, ETA for next update.

Appendix A — sample Prometheus / PromQL queries:

- Regional GPU util (avg over 2m):
  - avg by (region) (rate(gpu_tokens_served_total[2m])) / avg by (region) (gpu_capacity_tokens[2m])

- Error budget burn rate (windowed 1h):
  - (sum(increase(errors_total[1h])) by (route)) / (sum(increase(requests_total[1h])) by (route))

- Top noisy tenants (5m):
  - topk(10, sum by (tenant_id) (rate(requests_total[5m])))

Appendix B — quick-play checklist (one-page):

- Triage: open channel, snapshot dashboard, assign roles.
- Automated: enable burst, apply throttles, prime cache.
- Manual: staged model fallback, reduce token limits, suspend large jobs.
- Augment: activate reserved hosts, request cloud quota.
- Postmortem: collect artifacts, run replay, update playbook.

Notes & operational governance:

- All playbook actions must be annotated in the incident timeline and are subject to a weekly audit. Any exception to burst-pool fairness rules requires a post-incident justification and approval from SRE lead.
- This playbook is reviewed quarterly and after any major incident. Changes must be approved by the SRE manager and cross-reviewed with product for customer-experience implications.

Contact & escalation:

- Primary SRE pager: #sre-oncall (PagerDuty).
- Ops runbook owner: Marcus Wu (marcus@redwood.ai).
- Playbook CLI owner: Platform Tools (platform-tools@redwood.ai).
